x-tools.name: tdev_workspace
x-tools.description: Create, list and inspect development spaces; attach/detach enrolled projects, configure defaults and close. Membership selects projects, never grants authority. Empty spaces need no Git repository. Mutations use expectedRevision; close/detach retain source tasks and owned branches and require no open or uncertain tasks. Omit workspaceId when starting a task to use an automatic default space.

x-tools.name: tdev_task
x-tools.description: Start, inspect and manage an isolated source task for one project in a workspace. Start resolves project/base HEAD and owned branch naming. Omit workspaceId for an automatic default workspace; explicit workspaces use attached projects and their defaultRepo. Edit source with tdev_edit. Close retains branches; cleanup removes only an unchanged branch owned by this task. Continue a proved publication via start.fromTaskId. Start with localChanges=true to import the enrolled local checkout without writing to it. Integrate another same-project task delta with three-way merging; applied=false means the target is unchanged. Retry conflict resolution with new requestId and the returned sourceCheckpoint; keep prior resolutions if conflicts are truncated. Inspect includes outstanding processes independent of history pagination and dependency storage. resetEnvironment removes task dependencies/caches only after every execution is proved stopped; it also works after close. Close retains processes and dependencies.

x-tools.name: tdev_read
x-tools.description: Batch bounded immutable file/list/literal-search/diff/history reads at a checkpoint. Omit checkpoint to read the current committed task snapshot. Diff supports stat/patch/names, an accessible base checkpoint and byte pagination.

x-tools.name: tdev_edit
x-tools.description: Atomically edit files at expected checkpoint. Same request replays before stale checks.

x-tools.name: tdev_exec
x-tools.description: Run commands on Termux by default (same-UID developer authority, not a sandbox); explicit remote executor is optional. Returns a retained operation handle. Never resubmit with a new request after response loss. Native dependencies/caches persist per task through TDEV_ENV_DIR; use environment=fresh for a disposable environment. mode=process starts a foreground development server/debugger on a fixed checkpoint without blocking source edits or capturing its files; omit timeout to run until cancel/exit. Observe logs/stdin/cancel/retire through tdev_operation.

x-tools.name: tdev_operation
x-tools.description: Inspect any accepted operation by operationId or original request ID, including project and workspace changes. Status observes current progress without repeating effects. For exec/validation processes only: deliver sequenced stdin, request cancellation or retire stopped resources.

x-tools.name: tdev_validate
x-tools.description: Freeze an exact candidate commit and run the operator's mandatory command through trusted outer execution. With subject=artifact and artifactId, verifies retained bytes using adopted artifactValidation policy in fresh scratch; never alters source. Service packages additionally require a free loopback health port/path and exercise the manifest entrypoint with TDEV_PORT and X-Tdev-Release. Observe/log/cancel/retire through tdev_operation. Artifact validation cannot authorize source publication.

x-tools.name: tdev_publish
x-tools.description: Publish exactly the validated commit. Expected remote state is derived from its task when omitted; managed tasks create their branch only on first publication. Provider authentication belongs to the controller, not tdev_exec.

x-tools.name: tdev_project
x-tools.description: List projects and delegated policies; connect existing local Git folders or GitHub repositories, or create initialized projects. Local names are relative to the policy root; GitHub names are repository names under the policy owner. GitHub creation is private. Uses controller provider credentials; no gh authentication in exec needed. No caller-supplied credentials, commands or executor settings. Inspect original mutations through tdev_operation status.

x-tools.name: tdev_deploy
x-tools.description: Deploy a successfully validated native source candidate to a delegated Termux runit target. Release creates/updates a named owned service and checks process identity plus configured loopback HTTP readiness. Inspect returns current state and rotating logs; start/stop/rollback/remove require revision CAS. Remove preserves data/releases/logs. Observe interrupted effects through tdev_operation status before retrying. Source publication is separate; task dependency directories are not bundled. The app must return HTTP 200 with X-Tdev-Release equal to TDEV_RELEASE; writable state belongs in TDEV_DATA_DIR. Services must stay in the foreground. release subject=artifact uses a successful artifact validationId and manifest launch settings; command override is forbidden. health.port is the deployment port supplied as TDEV_PORT; health.path must match validation. Current artifact/runtime/policy checks precede stopping the previous service.

x-tools.name: tdev_artifact
x-tools.description: Inspect a recipe from successful source validation, prepare a retained native build, list builds or inspect sealed bytes. Default recipe path: tdev-package.json. prepare requires requestId and validationId; reuse the request after a lost reply. Uses fresh source, pinned public HTTPS dependencies and declared exports, independent of task caches and deployment targets. Observe/log/cancel/retire through tdev_operation; artifactId is the build operation id. list exposes outstanding builds regardless of history page. Build success is not artifact validation or deployment. Use tdev_validate subject=artifact for verification. Service inspect reports current declared runtime compatibility separately from retained-byte integrity; it never installs or starts a service. Export reads verified file bytes in bounded base64 pages, never writes caller paths. usage returns paged authorized retained-object counts, excluding scratch and deployment copies; shared digests can recur across pages. prunePreview reports live pins and retention policy; explicit prune requires its token and rechecks pins, journals retirement and preserves historical receipts. Active/previous deployments and unknown work cannot be pruned. No automatic GC.

x-tools.name: tdev_diagnostics
x-tools.description: Inspect your retained diagnostic incidents or acknowledge receipt by incidentId. Authorized diagnostic operators may activate bounded tracing (1–300 seconds; default 120) with requestId or stop it. Reuse requestId after a lost activation reply; replay within the 32-incident retention window does not extend expiry. Normal operation does not depend on diagnostics. Automatic watch reacts to dispatch/response failures, uncertain effects or slow dispatch candidates, never cancels/retries work. Alerts are offered in subsequent tool responses; acknowledgment does not prove user-visible delivery. No raw trace, credentials, commands or other principals’ incidents are returned. Activation and stop require the operator diagnostics grant.

x-semantics.oid: Raw full Git OID, repository object format determines length; checkpoint commit is CAS token.
x-semantics.requestId: Principal-scoped installation-lifetime dedup key. Same payload only; current auth precedes replay.

defaults.network: backend default: host for native; none for SSH/OCI
defaults.timeout: 300 seconds for command/validation; process has no deadline unless supplied
defaults.environment: task for native; fresh for remote

x-semantics.processStatus: Exactly one of operationId and lookupRequestId is required; neither/both rejected.
x-semantics.result: Task list/open/edit results, bounded query items, or retained operation. Operation contains id, kind, status, effect, result/error; running is independent of certainty. Output evidence fields are server-owned, never accepted as validation input.

execution.sourceMetadata: Private shallow Git checkpoint; no copied provider credentials. Validation HEAD starts at the frozen candidate commit; native validation rejects changed existing source and never imports test outputs.
execution.nativeBoundary: Same app UID, host network. Clean env and separate HOME/cwd are hygiene, not hostile-code isolation. Native code can access other same-UID files; use only code trusted with ordinary Termux user authority.
execution.nativeLimits: 1 MiB retained output; optional process deadline (required bounded command/validation deadline); CPU limit when a deadline is selected; 128 MiB file-size and 256 file-descriptor limits; sampled 128 MiB source/home/tmp and 2 GiB task dependency budgets (100000 files each). No hard aggregate memory/PID/disk quota. At most eight outstanding process-mode operations per task.
execution.nativeRecovery: Detached subreaper supervisor survives controller restart. Lost supervisor after dispatch without a sealed result remains uncertain, never automatically relaunched.

x-semantics.progress: task inspect reconciles its busy operation and up to eight outstanding snapshot processes independently of history pagination, then reads bounded operation page and live remote head. Observation cursor hashes the returned facts, timestamps delimit observation (not atomic cross-provider snapshot). since equal means checked now/no change, not stalled proof; wait at least pollAfterMs or do independent work. Mutation prerequisites are rechecked at admission. Closed tasks discoverable with includeClosed. Process status since opts into freshness. Replaying a mutation reconciles original identity, never repeats the effect.
x-semantics.annotations: Fixed tmcp host hints: all advertised tools set readOnlyHint=true and the other hints=false. Hints do not grant authority; core still enforces mutation identity, authorization, validation and publication.
x-semantics.managedProjects: Policies delegate local-root or GitHub-owner project connect/create with current operator validation/tooling. Start resolves defaults once; first publish uses absence CAS. Close retains refs; cleanup needs ownership and exact last published OID, works after close, and never adopts existing refs. Delegated projects publish only managed branches.
x-semantics.composition: Workspace membership binds enrolled project identity without granting permissions. taskId selects a source task; workspaceId selects composition. Omitted workspaceId creates/reuses the principal default workspace atomically during task admission. Explicit membership/defaults are rechecked at admission. close/detach reject open or pending tasks; closed tasks and cleanup evidence remain inspectable. Workspace mutations commit state and replay result together with expectedRevision CAS.
x-semantics.sourceIntegration: localChanges=true on start captures the enrolled checkout final tracked plus nonignored untracked bytes into a new source task, preserving user index/refs/files. Matching HEAD/ref and two equal scans detect observed races; no atomic filesystem snapshot is claimed. integrate freezes the same-project source checkpoint at admission and applies its delta from source base, requiring that base to precede the target base. Conflicts return applied=false without changing target source; explicit resolutions apply atomically. Source-task lineage is retained in the operation, not added as Git merge parents; exact frozen validation/publication rules remain unchanged.

x-mcp.legacy: Core HTTP: No initialize/initialized, session IDs, GET/DELETE streams, SSE replay or automatic downgrade. No advertised subscriptions, MRTR input requests or task extension.
